results.evidence: dist_km is the one-way approach, not a round-trip total, so the reader's comparison with the 38.5-mi itinerary sum doesn't hold. 38.6 km (about 24 mi) could be the one-way distance on foot if a party walks the roughly 7-mile lakeshore trail instead of taking the boat, and twice that is the 48-mi top of the totalNote range. The row's own trailhead note mentions that walk. The boat-based itinerary puts the walk nearer 16-17 mi one way. The Ross Lake Resort pages give no mileages, and no source states a one-way distance to the base of Mongo Ridge. To settle it: a source stating the one-way distance from Ross Dam to the ridge base, with or without the boat.

results.fact: Total gain vs loss on a round trip
results.evidence: The itinerary days add up to exactly gain_ft (10,000) and loss_ft (10,700). A car-to-car trip can't lose more than it gains, and the walk from the 2,100-ft trailhead down to the dock would, if anything, push the gain above the loss. The retry found no source stating this route's car-to-car loss or gain, only the earlier Luna/Fury survey trip's roughly 10,000 ft of gain, which is a different route. Under the rules, loss_ft isn't set equal to gain_ft and the itinerary days aren't rebalanced. To settle it: a source stating this route's total car-to-car gain and loss.

The resort's water-taxi pages list no fixed pickup times from Ross Dam, so neither the 8:00 AM start nor the ~2:00 PM boat can be checked against a published schedule. The only party account (second ascent) took a 2 PM boat and camped in the Access Creek basin the same evening, so a 2 PM boat with an evening arrival is possible, though 7 PM is tight for 11.5 mi of trail plus the bushwhack. No source gives times to replace the schedule. To settle it: published taxi departure times, or a trip report with times for the landing-to-basin day.

The 14-mi figures (turnaround, dist_km, the 28.4-mi round trip) describe the Staircase approach. The WTA North Fork Skokomish page puts First Divide at 13.1 mi from Staircase, so those three agree. The ~29 mi in approach and descent_text is the Duckabush/Marmot Lake approach, which the text labels as a different approach. Published segment distances (6.2 mi to the park boundary, about 10.3 mi on to the junction, and 2.9 mi from the Duckabush trail up to First Divide per the WTA page) put First Divide about 19.4 mi from the Duckabush trailhead going direct. The Marmot Lake detour adds several miles, so 29 may be too high, but no source states a one-way distance to Hopper from the Duckabush. To settle it: a trip report or guide giving the Duckabush trailhead-to-Hopper distance.

results.fact: Where the Mount Hopper Way leaves the trail / high camp
results.evidence: One source puts the Mount Hopper Way junction 12.4 mi up the North Fork Skokomish trail, about 2 mi below the summit. A 2021 trip report had the party go back DOWN the trail from First Divide and leave it 'in the vicinity of where the Hopper Way trail was marked on the map'. That points to a junction below the divide, not at it, but gives no elevation or distance. Mileage conventions for First Divide differ (12.5 mi in one source, 13.1 in another), so 12.4 mi could be right at the divide or 0.7 mi below it. Neither 'at First Divide' nor 'near Two Bear Camp at about 3,680 ft' has two agreeing sources. To settle it: the junction's elevation or position from a topo map or a trip report.

The only published total is 4,400 ft (with 32 mi) for the COMBINED Steel and Hopper trip. WTA's Hopper page lists 6,114 ft, which is just the summit elevation, not a car-to-car gain. The itinerary adds up to 5,290 ft, and loss_ft and totalNote agree with it. No outside source states a car-to-car gain for Hopper alone, and the rules forbid computing a new gain_ft. To settle it: a source stating the Staircase-to-Hopper round-trip gain.
